questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental component of a data communication system?
questions.explanation: The five essential components of a data communication system are the message, sender (transmitter), receiver, transmission medium, and protocol.

questions.question: What is the standard definition of Bandwidth in computer networking?

options.label: A
options.text: The physical thickness of a transmission wire

options.label: B
options.text: The volume of data transferred over a channel per unit of time (data transfer rate)

options.label: C
options.text: The total electrical resistance of a network cable

options.label: D
options.text: The number of computers connected to a server

questions.correct_answer_text: The volume of data transferred over a channel per unit of time (data transfer rate)
questions.explanation: Bandwidth refers to the data transmission capacity or rate of data transfer through a communication channel, typically measured in bits per second (bps).

questions.question: Which bandwidth category provides data transmission speeds of 1 Mbps or higher?
questions.explanation: Broadband offers high-speed data transmission typically defined as 1 Mbps or above, whereas narrowband operates at 45-300 bps and voiceband reaches up to 9600 bps.

questions.question: What is the loss of signal strength as it travels through a transmission medium known as?
questions.explanation: Attenuation is the gradual loss of signal intensity or amplitude as an electrical or optical wave propagates through a medium over distance.

questions.question: A telecommunication channel transferring data at 10 Mbps transmits how many bits each second?
questions.explanation: 1 Mbps = 1,000,000 bits per second (10^6 bps). Therefore, 10 Mbps equals 10,000,000 bits per second.

questions.question: Which data transmission mode permits data to travel in only one predetermined direction at all times?
questions.explanation: In Simplex mode, communication is strictly unidirectional; the transmitter only sends data and the receiver only receives it (e.g., commercial radio broadcast).

questions.question: A Walkie-Talkie system where both parties can talk but only one at a time is an example of:
questions.explanation: In Half-Duplex mode, both devices can transmit and receive data, but not simultaneously; only one direction is active at any given moment.

questions.question: Which transmission mode allows simultaneous two-way real-time voice communication, as in a cellular telephone call?
questions.explanation: In Full-Duplex mode, both connected parties can send and receive data at the same time without waiting for each other to stop transmitting.

questions.question: Sending data from a single sender to a specific chosen group of multiple recipients is known as:
questions.explanation: Multicast delivers data packets from one source to a defined group of interested destination hosts, unlike broadcast which sends to all nodes.

questions.question: Sending television signals from a transmitter tower to every home television antenna across a city is an example of:
questions.explanation: Television transmission is broadcast (sent to all receivers in range) and simplex (signals flow in one direction only with no reply from TV sets).

questions.question: In which transmission method is data transmitted character-by-character accompanied by start and stop bits?
questions.explanation: Asynchronous transmission transmits one character (byte) at a time, framing each byte with a Start bit (logic 0) and one or more Stop bits (logic 1).

questions.question: What is the typical value of the Start bit in standard asynchronous serial communication?
questions.explanation: In asynchronous transmission, an idle line stays at high voltage (1). A Start bit transitions the line to low voltage (0) to alert the receiver.

questions.question: Which transmission method groups large numbers of characters into synchronized blocks or frames for high efficiency?
questions.explanation: Synchronous transmission sends continuous blocks of data synchronized by a shared master clock signal, eliminating individual start/stop overhead.

questions.question: Which data transmission method guarantees a fixed time interval between successive data packets, making it ideal for live video streaming?
questions.explanation: Isochronous transmission combines features of synchronous and asynchronous methods, ensuring fixed, regular packet delivery without jitter for live streaming.

questions.question: If an 8-bit character is sent with 1 start bit and 1 stop bit in asynchronous mode, what is the transmission efficiency?
questions.explanation: Total bits sent = 1 start + 8 data + 1 stop = 10 bits. Efficiency = (Useful data bits / Total bits) * 100% = (8 / 10) * 100% = 80%.

questions.question: Why are copper wire pairs twisted around each other in Twisted Pair cables?

options.label: A
options.text: To increase the tensile breaking strength of the cable

options.label: B
options.text: To reduce electromagnetic interference (EMI) and crosstalk between pairs

options.label: C
options.text: To increase electrical capacitance and current flow

questions.correct_answer_text: To reduce electromagnetic interference (EMI) and crosstalk between pairs
questions.explanation: Twisting the two conductor wires cancels out external electromagnetic noise and minimizes crosstalk from adjacent wire pairs.

questions.question: Which registered jack modular connector is standard for terminating UTP Ethernet network cables?
questions.explanation: RJ-45 (8-pin modular connector) is the worldwide standard connector used for terminating twisted pair cables in Ethernet local area networks.

questions.question: Which physical principle governs the propagation of light pulses along the glass core of an optical fiber cable?
questions.explanation: Light signals travel through optical fibers by Total Internal Reflection, occurring because the central glass core has a higher refractive index than the surrounding cladding.

questions.question: Which concentric layer of an optical fiber cable has a lower refractive index than the core to keep light trapped inside?
questions.explanation: The cladding surrounds the core and has a lower refractive index, satisfying the condition required for total internal reflection of light rays.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of Optical Fiber Cable over copper Twisted Pair cable?

options.label: A
options.text: Complete immunity to electromagnetic interference (EMI) and radio frequency noise

options.label: B
options.text: Ability to be spliced easily with simple household pliers

options.label: C
options.text: Lower initial purchasing and installation cost than UTP

options.label: D
options.text: Conduction of high-voltage direct electric current

questions.correct_answer_text: Complete immunity to electromagnetic interference (EMI) and radio frequency noise
questions.explanation: Because optical fibers transmit information as photons of light rather than electrical currents, they are completely immune to electromagnetic and RF interference.

questions.question: Which electromagnetic wave spectrum travels omnidirectionally and can penetrate solid walls and buildings easily?
questions.explanation: Radio waves have relatively low frequencies and long wavelengths, enabling them to travel in all directions (omnidirectional) and penetrate obstacles like walls.

questions.question: Why do terrestrial microwave communication towers require strict line-of-sight (LOS) alignment?

options.label: A
options.text: Because high-frequency microwave signals travel in straight beams and do not bend around obstacles

options.label: B
options.text: Because they only function during direct sunlight hours

options.label: C
options.text: Because microwaves are converted into acoustic sound waves in air

options.label: D
options.text: To prevent interference with submarine cables

questions.correct_answer_text: Because high-frequency microwave signals travel in straight beams and do not bend around obstacles
questions.explanation: Microwaves travel along straight line-of-sight paths; antennas must face each other directly and be placed on high towers to overcome the curvature of Earth.

questions.question: At approximately what altitude above Earth's equator do Geostationary Communication Satellites orbit?
questions.explanation: Geostationary satellites orbit at approximately 35,786 km (about 36,000 km) above Earth's equator, matching Earth's 24-hour rotational period.

questions.question: Which wireless medium is commonly used in television remote controllers and cannot pass through solid walls?
questions.explanation: Infrared light has very high frequency and short wavelength; it cannot penetrate opaque barriers like walls, making it secure and ideal for TV remotes.

questions.question: What is Bangladesh's first communication satellite placed in geostationary orbit named?
questions.explanation: Bangabandhu Satellite-1 (BS-1) was launched on May 11, 2018, positioned at 119.1° East longitude as Bangladesh's first geostationary communications satellite.

questions.question: Which IEEE standard governs Bluetooth wireless communication technology?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth technology is standardized under IEEE 802.15.1 for short-range Wireless Personal Area Networks (WPAN) operating in the 2.4 GHz band.

questions.question: What is the typical operating radius for standard Class 2 Bluetooth devices like wireless earphones?
questions.explanation: Class 2 Bluetooth devices, used in mobile phones and wireless accessories, typically operate within an effective range of about 10 meters (33 feet).

questions.question: Which IEEE standard specifies Wireless Local Area Networks (WLAN), popularly known as Wi-Fi?
questions.explanation: The IEEE 802.11 standard family governs Wi-Fi wireless local area network technologies.

questions.question: Which wireless broadband technology is defined by IEEE 802.16 and provides metropolitan area coverage up to 50 km?
questions.explanation: WiMAX (Worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access) is based on IEEE 802.16 and delivers high-speed wireless broadband over metropolitan distances.

questions.question: Which ultra-short-range wireless technology operates within 4 to 10 centimeters for contactless payment cards and smartphone taps?
questions.explanation: Near Field Communication (NFC) operates at 13.56 MHz over distances of 4 cm or less, facilitating fast and secure contactless point-of-sale transactions.

questions.question: Which was the defining technical characteristic of First Generation (1G) mobile cellular networks?

options.label: A
options.text: Analog voice signal transmission with no data or SMS capability

options.label: B
options.text: High-definition video streaming over packet networks

options.label: C
options.text: Ultra-low millisecond latency for autonomous driving

questions.correct_answer_text: Analog voice signal transmission with no data or SMS capability
questions.explanation: 1G cellular systems (e.g., AMPS) relied entirely on analog frequency modulation for voice calls only, with no digital encryption or text messaging.

questions.question: Short Message Service (SMS) and digital cellular encryption were first introduced in which mobile generation?
questions.explanation: 2G networks (GSM and CDMA) introduced digital transmission, SIM cards, international roaming, and Short Message Service (SMS).

questions.question: Which mobile network generation first made seamless mobile video calling and mobile broadband internet widespread?
questions.explanation: 3G (UMTS, WCDMA, EV-DO) introduced packet-based mobile broadband speeds exceeding 384 Kbps to several Mbps, enabling mobile video calls and web browsing.

questions.question: Which core technology standard powers Fourth Generation (4G) high-speed mobile networks?
questions.explanation: 4G networks are built on LTE and LTE-Advanced architectures, using an all-IP packet-switched network to deliver mobile data speeds exceeding 100 Mbps.

questions.question: What is a primary performance objective of 5G cellular networks compared to 4G?

options.label: A
options.text: Ultra-low latency below 1 millisecond and massive IoT connectivity

options.label: C
options.text: Restricting connections to voice calls only

questions.correct_answer_text: Ultra-low latency below 1 millisecond and massive IoT connectivity
questions.explanation: 5G offers multi-gigabit peak data speeds, massive machine-type communications (connecting millions of IoT devices per km²), and ultra-low latency (<1 ms).

topics.topic_name: Computer Network Classifications (PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN)

questions.question: Connecting a smartphone to a wireless Bluetooth headset within a personal workspace is an example of which network type?
questions.explanation: A Personal Area Network (PAN) covers a small area centered around an individual person, typically within a radius of 10 meters.

questions.question: A network interconnecting computers located within a single college building or computer lab is classified as a:
questions.explanation: A Local Area Network (LAN) spans a geographically limited area such as a home, office suite, laboratory, or school campus.

questions.question: A cable television network distributing signals across an entire metropolitan city is an example of:
questions.explanation: A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) spans an entire municipality or city, larger than a LAN but smaller than a nationwide WAN.

questions.question: What is the largest and most well-known example of a Wide Area Network (WAN) in the world?
questions.explanation: The global Internet connects millions of computers, networks, and servers across all continents, representing the ultimate Wide Area Network (WAN).

questions.question: A private, secure computer network accessible only by authorized internal employees of an organization is called an:
questions.explanation: An intranet is a private internal enterprise network restricted strictly to employees to share information and computing resources securely.

questions.question: In which network topology are all workstations connected to a single common backbone cable terminated at both ends?
questions.explanation: Bus topology uses a single central backbone transmission line to which all network nodes tap into, with terminators at both ends to absorb signals.

questions.question: Which topology connects all peripheral nodes directly to a central hub or switch device?
questions.explanation: In star topology, every host computer has a point-to-point connection to a central multiport switch or hub.

questions.question: What happens if the central switch fails in a Star Topology network?

options.label: C
options.text: The network automatically transforms into a Bus topology

questions.explanation: Because the central hub/switch is the single point of coordination and relay, its failure brings down communication for all connected devices.

questions.question: How many physical links are required in a fully connected Mesh topology having n nodes?
questions.explanation: In a full mesh topology, every node connects directly to every other node. The total number of duplex links is given by n(n - 1) / 2.

questions.question: A network formed by interconnecting multiple Star networks along a central Bus backbone is called a:
questions.explanation: A tree topology arranges nodes hierarchically, where multiple secondary star networks are grouped and connected to a primary backbone trunk.

questions.question: What primary function does a Modem perform in data communication?

options.label: A
options.text: Converts digital signals to analog (modulation) and analog to digital (demodulation)

options.label: B
options.text: Amplifies optical light pulses inside fiber cables

options.label: C
options.text: Scans computer files for software viruses

questions.correct_answer_text: Converts digital signals to analog (modulation) and analog to digital (demodulation)
questions.explanation: Modem stands for MOdulator-DEModulator; it translates digital computer data into analog audio/radio waves for transmission over lines and vice-versa.

questions.question: What is the crucial operational distinction between a network Hub and an intelligent network Switch?

options.label: A
options.text: A hub broadcasts incoming packets to all connected ports, while a switch directs packets to the specific target MAC address

options.label: B
options.text: A hub operates on fiber optic cables while a switch only uses copper

options.label: C
options.text: A hub has an internal routing table while a switch does not

options.label: D
options.text: A switch cannot connect more than two computers

questions.correct_answer_text: A hub broadcasts incoming packets to all connected ports, while a switch directs packets to the specific target MAC address
questions.explanation: A hub broadcasts data to every port causing collisions, while an intelligent switch reads destination MAC addresses and forwards packets only to the specific recipient port.

questions.question: Which OSI layer device inspects destination IP addresses to route data packets between two different logical networks?
questions.explanation: A router operates at the Network Layer (Layer 3), using IP addresses and routing algorithms to forward data packets across disparate networks.

questions.question: Which internetworking device connects two networks that run on completely different communication protocols and architectures?
questions.explanation: A gateway acts as a protocol converter, translating data between networks that use entirely different protocols and network architectures.

questions.question: What is the permanent 48-bit physical hardware address burned into every Network Interface Card (NIC) called?
questions.explanation: A MAC (Media Access Control) address is a unique 48-bit (6-byte) hexadecimal identifier assigned permanently to network interface hardware by manufacturers.
